title: WHY AFRICAN PENGUINS KEEP COMBING THEIR FEATHERS
caption: African penguins have a reason for all that grooming. 🐧 #AfricanPenguin #OceanLife #Wildlife #WildVox

narration_timeline.text: Why does this African penguin keep combing its feathers with its bill?
narration_timeline.scene: African penguins actively combing plumage at Betty's Bay.

narration_timeline.text: Along southern Africa's coast, these birds move between ocean feeding trips and land.
narration_timeline.scene: African penguins in their authentic coastal colony, plus walking footage.

narration_timeline.text: Back ashore, they preen, cleaning and lining up their tightly packed feathers.
narration_timeline.scene: African penguins visibly grooming with their bills.

narration_timeline.text: That feather layer helps keep cold seawater away from the skin.
narration_timeline.scene: African penguin coastal group; explain feather insulation without false microscopic overlay.

narration_timeline.text: But they also need safe places on land where they can shelter and breed.
narration_timeline.scene: African penguins near an actual den at Stony Point.

narration_timeline.text: So the constant grooming is more than fussing. It's upkeep for a life split between sea and shore.
narration_timeline.scene: Authentic portrait African penguin walking from shore toward the sea, first seconds of Boulders Beach source, followed by distinct colony footage.
